title: Understanding the Objective Function
text: The objective function $R(\theta_1)$ is given as $R(\theta_1)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}**{n}x_i(y_i-\theta_1x_i)**{2}$. This function represents the average of the squared differences between the observed rides $y_i$ and the predicted rides $\theta_1x_i$, weighted by $x_i$.

title: Differentiating the Objective Function
text: To find the derivative of $R(\theta_1)$ with respect to $\theta_1$, apply the chain rule to the expression $x_i(y_i-\theta_1x_i)**{2}$.

title: Applying the Chain Rule
text: Differentiate the inner function $y_i-\theta_1x_i$ with respect to $\theta_1$. What do you get?

title: Differentiating the Outer Function
text: Now, differentiate the outer function $(y_i-\theta_1x_i)**{2}$ with respect to $y_i-\theta_1x_i$. What is the result?

title: Combining the Derivatives
text: Combine the derivatives from the previous steps using the chain rule to find the derivative of $x_i(y_i-\theta_1x_i)**{2}$ with respect to $\theta_1$.

title: Summing Over All Observations
text: Sum the derivative $-2*x_i*(y_i-\theta_1*x_i)$ over all observations $i$ from $$1$$ to $n$. What is the result?

title: Final Derivative Expression
text: Divide the summed expression by $n$ to find the derivative of $R(\theta_1)$ with respect to $\theta_1$.
